title: Flechtwerk — F1 Live Timing
description: A pit wall over the live-timing tape. Every state panel computes an AS-OF CURSOR and filters event_time <= cursor with no lower bound; series panels additionally apply the time range. That one mechanism gives three modes with no special cases: a now-relative range with auto-refresh is LIVE, an absolute range end dragged through a past race is SCRUB, and mode=replay advances a virtual clock at ${speed}×. No timestamp is ever rewritten — only the cursor moves. Open a session from 'Flechtwerk — F1 Season' to get its window and replay link filled in.

list.name: session
list.label: Session

query.rawSql: SELECT session_key AS __value, label AS __text FROM flechtwerk.f1_sessions FINAL ORDER BY start_utc DESC, session_key DESC

list.description: Which session's tape to read. Newest first, so a live weekend surfaces at the top. The value is the archive's numeric session key — the one column every table is filtered by.

query.rawSql: SELECT DISTINCT racing_number AS __value, tla AS __text FROM flechtwerk.f1_drivers FINAL WHERE session_key = ${session} ORDER BY tla

list.name: mode
list.label: Mode
list.description: wall: the cursor is the end of the dashboard's time range — a now-relative range with auto-refresh IS live mode, and dragging an absolute range end through a past race IS scrub mode. replay: a virtual clock advances the cursor at ${speed}× from ${race_start_ms}. Nothing is ever re-timestamped; only the cursor moves.

list.name: play_ms
list.label: Play From (ms)
list.description: Wall-clock epoch ms at which a replay was started — filled by the season dashboard's '▶ replay' link. Only read when mode = replay.

list.name: race_start_ms
list.label: Race Start (ms)
list.description: Event-time epoch ms the replay's virtual clock starts from — filled by the season dashboard's '▶ replay' link. Only read when mode = replay.

target.rawSql: SELECT toUnixTimestamp64Milli(started_at) AS time, toUnixTimestamp64Milli(coalesce(ended_at, now64(3))) AS timeEnd, label AS text FROM flechtwerk.f1_track_status FINAL WHERE session_key = ${session} AND label != 'AllClear' ORDER BY started_at

panels.title: Race Wall — The Leaderboard, as of the Cursor
panels.description: One row per driver, each field the LATEST value at or before the cursor (argMax over event_time). There is deliberately no lower time bound: a driver's last update may predate the visible range, and a leaderboard that forgets a car in the pits is worse than useless. `gap`/`intvl` are the feed's own strings — '+1.234' seconds, '1L' a lap down, 'LAP 24' for the leader — kept verbatim because that is what a pit wall reads; the parsed seconds live alongside them. `catching` is the upstream's own judgement that this car is closing.

targets.rawSql:
WITH if('${mode}' = 'replay',
        fromUnixTimestamp64Milli(toInt64(${race_start_ms}
          + (toUnixTimestamp64Milli(now64(3)) - ${play_ms}) * ${speed})),
        fromUnixTimestamp64Milli(toInt64(${__to}))) AS cursor
SELECT argMax(position, event_time)               AS pos,
       argMax(tla, event_time)                    AS drv,
       racing_number                              AS num,
       argMax(gap_raw, event_time)                AS gap,
       argMax(interval_raw, event_time)           AS intvl,
       argMax(interval_s, event_time)             AS intvl_s,
       argMax(catching, event_time)               AS catching,
       if(argMax(last_lap_ms, event_time) IS NULL, '', concat(toString(intDiv(argMax(last_lap_ms, event_time), 60000)), ':',
       leftPad(toString(intDiv(argMax(last_lap_ms, event_time) % 60000, 1000)), 2, '0'), '.',
       leftPad(toString(argMax(last_lap_ms, event_time) % 1000), 3, '0'))) AS last_lap,
       if(argMax(best_lap_ms, event_time) IS NULL, '', concat(toString(intDiv(argMax(best_lap_ms, event_time), 60000)), ':',
       leftPad(toString(intDiv(argMax(best_lap_ms, event_time) % 60000, 1000)), 2, '0'), '.',
       leftPad(toString(argMax(best_lap_ms, event_time) % 1000), 3, '0'))) AS best_lap,
       argMax(sector1_ms, event_time) / 1000      AS s1,
       argMax(sector2_ms, event_time) / 1000      AS s2,
       argMax(sector3_ms, event_time) / 1000      AS s3,
       argMax(tyre_compound, event_time)          AS tyre,
       argMax(tyre_age, event_time)               AS age,
       argMax(stint, event_time)                  AS stint,
       argMax(pit_count, event_time)              AS stops,
       argMax(speed_st, event_time)               AS top_kph,
       multiIf(argMax(retired, event_time), 'RETIRED',
               argMax(stopped, event_time), 'STOPPED',
               argMax(in_pit, event_time),  'PIT',
               argMax(pit_out, event_time), 'OUT', '')  AS status
FROM flechtwerk.f1_standings
WHERE session_key = ${session} AND event_time <= cursor
GROUP BY racing_number
HAVING pos > 0
ORDER BY pos

panels.title: Track Status
panels.description: The flag state at the cursor, from the 585-byte TrackStatus feed the board folds into every leaderboard row and every lap. Twelve records decide whether a whole race's lap times mean anything.

targets.rawSql:
WITH if('${mode}' = 'replay',
        fromUnixTimestamp64Milli(toInt64(${race_start_ms}
          + (toUnixTimestamp64Milli(now64(3)) - ${play_ms}) * ${speed})),
        fromUnixTimestamp64Milli(toInt64(${__to}))) AS cursor
SELECT argMax(label, event_time) AS flag
FROM flechtwerk.f1_track_status
WHERE session_key = ${session} AND started_at <= cursor

panels.title: Lap / Session Clock
panels.description: From the LapCount and ExtrapolatedClock feeds. `total_laps` is sent ONCE, with the first LapCount record, so the board folds it into state rather than reading the latest patch — which is why this panel still knows the race distance on lap 60. LapCount is a race-only feed: in practice and qualifying these read empty, by nature.

targets.rawSql:
WITH if('${mode}' = 'replay',
        fromUnixTimestamp64Milli(toInt64(${race_start_ms}
          + (toUnixTimestamp64Milli(now64(3)) - ${play_ms}) * ${speed})),
        fromUnixTimestamp64Milli(toInt64(${__to}))) AS cursor
SELECT argMax(lap, event_time) AS lap, argMax(total_laps, event_time) AS total_laps,
       argMax(remaining_s, event_time) AS remaining_s
FROM flechtwerk.f1_clock
WHERE session_key = ${session} AND event_time <= cursor

panels.title: Tape Freshness
panels.description: Seconds between the cursor and the last Heartbeat line before it. The Heartbeat feed beats every ~15 s no matter what is happening on track, so this distinguishes 'the session is under a red flag and nothing is moving' from 'the ingest stage died' — a distinction the leaderboard alone cannot make. During a backfill or a scrub it reads ~15 s; while live it also carries the poll interval and the CDN's own delay.

targets.rawSql:
WITH if('${mode}' = 'replay',
        fromUnixTimestamp64Milli(toInt64(${race_start_ms}
          + (toUnixTimestamp64Milli(now64(3)) - ${play_ms}) * ${speed})),
        fromUnixTimestamp64Milli(toInt64(${__to}))) AS cursor
SELECT dateDiff('second', max(event_time), cursor) AS behind_s
FROM flechtwerk.f1_heartbeats
WHERE session_key = ${session} AND event_time <= cursor

panels.title: Gap to the Leader (s)
panels.description: Every gap update the feed sent, as it sent it. This is a *series* panel, so unlike the leaderboard above it does apply the dashboard's time range — the shape of a race is a window, not an instant. Lapped cars simply drop out: their gap is expressed in laps, and the board deliberately keeps laps and seconds in separate columns rather than inventing a duration for them.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT event_time AS time, tla, gap_s
FROM flechtwerk.f1_standings
WHERE session_key = ${session} AND racing_number IN (${drivers})
  AND gap_s IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(event_time)
ORDER BY event_time

panels.title: Lap Times (s) — Flags Annotated
panels.description: One point per completed lap. The yellow regions are the flag periods the board derived from TrackStatus, so the slow laps explain themselves: a lap behind a virtual safety car is not a lap. Every point also carries `clean` and `track_status` columns in the table below, which is what a pace analysis filters on rather than eyeballing this.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT event_time AS time, tla, lap_ms / 1000 AS lap_s
FROM flechtwerk.f1_laps
WHERE session_key = ${session} AND racing_number IN (${drivers})
  AND lap_ms IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(event_time)
ORDER BY event_time

panels.title: Battle Radar — Within One Second of the Car Ahead
panels.description: The interesting part of a leaderboard is who is *closing*. `catching` comes straight from the feed (IntervalToPositionAhead.Catching), so no series has to be differentiated to find it. Rows appear and vanish as the cursor moves — this is the leaderboard state, filtered, not a separate stream.

targets.rawSql:
WITH if('${mode}' = 'replay',
        fromUnixTimestamp64Milli(toInt64(${race_start_ms}
          + (toUnixTimestamp64Milli(now64(3)) - ${play_ms}) * ${speed})),
        fromUnixTimestamp64Milli(toInt64(${__to}))) AS cursor
SELECT pos, drv, iv.1 AS intvl, round(iv.2, 3) AS gap_s,
       catching, tyre, age
FROM (
    SELECT argMax(position, event_time)                     AS pos,
           argMax(tla, event_time)                          AS drv,
           argMax((interval_raw, interval_s), event_time)   AS iv,
           argMax(catching, event_time)                     AS catching,
           argMax(tyre_compound, event_time)                AS tyre,
           argMax(tyre_age, event_time)                     AS age,
           argMax(retired, event_time)                      AS retired
    FROM flechtwerk.f1_standings
    WHERE session_key = ${session} AND event_time <= cursor
    GROUP BY racing_number)
WHERE iv.1 LIKE '+%' AND iv.2 IS NOT NULL AND iv.2 < 1.0 AND NOT retired AND pos > 0
ORDER BY pos

panels.title: Pit Stops
panels.description: `stationary_s` is what the crew is judged on; `pit_lane_s` is what the strategist pays. The difference — ~20 s of pit-lane speed limit — is the real cost of a stop and the number that decides a one-stop from a two-stop. Each row is event-timed by the stop's own upstream Timestamp, not by the tape offset that delivered it.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT p.event_time AS time, d.tla AS drv, p.lap,
       p.stationary_s, p.pit_lane_s
FROM flechtwerk.f1_pit_stops AS p
LEFT JOIN (SELECT racing_number, tla FROM flechtwerk.f1_drivers FINAL
           WHERE session_key = ${session}) AS d USING (racing_number)
WHERE p.session_key = ${session}
ORDER BY p.event_time DESC

panels.title: Race Control
panels.description: Every message race control broadcast, newest first — flags, safety cars, DRS, penalties. The RaceControlMessages feed opens the session with an ARRAY of the messages so far and switches to index-keyed DICTS a few lines in; the board accepts both, which is why this list has no gap at the transition.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT event_time AS time, message_text AS message, flag, lap
FROM flechtwerk.f1_race_control
WHERE session_key = ${session}
ORDER BY event_time DESC

panels.title: Weather
panels.description: ~one sample a minute. Track temperature runs 20 °C above the air and is the number that actually decides tyre behaviour. Every field arrives from the feed as a STRING ('30.0'), which is why the board coerces rather than casts.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT event_time AS time, air_temp, track_temp, humidity, wind_speed
FROM flechtwerk.f1_weather
WHERE session_key = ${session} AND $__timeFilter(event_time)
ORDER BY event_time

panels.title: Speed Trap (km/h) — Best So Far
panels.description: The fastest reading each driver has posted at the longest straight's trap, as of the cursor. A `max` rather than an argMax: unlike a gap, a top speed is a session record and not a state.

targets.rawSql:
WITH if('${mode}' = 'replay',
        fromUnixTimestamp64Milli(toInt64(${race_start_ms}
          + (toUnixTimestamp64Milli(now64(3)) - ${play_ms}) * ${speed})),
        fromUnixTimestamp64Milli(toInt64(${__to}))) AS cursor
SELECT argMax(tla, event_time) AS drv, max(speed_st) AS top_kph
FROM flechtwerk.f1_standings
WHERE session_key = ${session} AND event_time <= cursor AND speed_st IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY racing_number
ORDER BY top_kph DESC
LIMIT 12

panels.title: Track Map (Telemetry-Gated)
panels.description: Sixty seconds of position samples up to the cursor, coloured by age — so the fading tail draws the circuit and the bright heads are the cars. Coordinates are the upstream's own frame: no projection, no documented origin, no units, which is fine for the one thing this is for. Requires the session to have been requested WITH telemetry; the two .z feeds are two thirds of the download, so `--no-telemetry` skips them and this stays empty. Cars sitting in the garage report exactly (0, 0) and are filtered out.

targets.rawSql:
WITH if('${mode}' = 'replay',
        fromUnixTimestamp64Milli(toInt64(${race_start_ms}
          + (toUnixTimestamp64Milli(now64(3)) - ${play_ms}) * ${speed})),
        fromUnixTimestamp64Milli(toInt64(${__to}))) AS cursor
SELECT x, y, dateDiff('second', event_time, cursor) AS age_s
FROM flechtwerk.f1_positions
WHERE session_key = ${session} AND status = 'OnTrack'
  AND event_time <= cursor AND event_time > cursor - INTERVAL 60 SECOND
  AND (x != 0 OR y != 0)
ORDER BY age_s DESC
